definition: The practice of splitting documents into retrieval units based on semantic coherence (like topic or section boundaries) rather than a fixed number of characters or tokens.
details: Semantic chunking aims to improve retrieval-augmented generation quality by keeping semantically related content together in the same chunk, rather than arbitrarily cutting sentences or ideas in half.
story: Think of a grammar teacher who never memorized a rule but can still tell you when a sentence sounds wrong. Here is the short version: The practice of splitting documents into retrieval units based on semantic coherence (like topic or section boundaries) rather than a fixed number of characters or tokens. The part that makes it sing: Semantic chunking aims to improve retrieval-augmented generation quality by keeping semantically related content together in the same chunk, rather than arbitrarily cutting sentences or ideas in half. The machine learns to read between the lines by reading an impossible number of lines. And that is Semantic Chunking — teaching a machine to read between the lines.
